examples.name: Default
examples.summary: Default field with label, input, and helper text.

examples.name: Sizes
examples.summary: All three size variants side by side (small 28px, medium 32px, large 40px input height).

examples.name: Required
examples.summary: Required state — the `Label` shows the Required tag, the input receives native `required` + `aria-required`, and the helper adopts the warning tone.

examples.name: Invalid
examples.summary: Invalid state — the helper switches to `kind="invalid"` (danger tokens) and the input gets the invalid border/ring plus `aria-invalid`.

examples.name: Disabled
examples.summary: Disabled state — the input is disabled, the helper switches to `kind="disabled"` (lock icon), and the label dims via the inherited muted text token.

examples.name: Icons
examples.summary: `#iconLeft` and `#iconRight` slots are forwarded to the underlying `InputText`, shown with a leading icon, a trailing icon, and both.

examples.name: Login
examples.summary: The e-mail field of a sign-in form. `type="email"`, `autocomplete="username"` and `spellcheck="false"` land on the `<input>`, so the browser and password managers recognise the login field.

examples.name: ReadOnly
examples.summary: A value the user can read and copy but never change (an ID, a generated key) is `readonly`: transparent, dashed border, no hover — next to an editable field it never looks editable. Use `disabled` only for a control that is temporarily unavailable.
